Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:6909
Court No. - 75
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1239 of 2020
Applicant :- Sukhbir

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rama Shankar Mishra,Adarsh Kumar Bajpai (Amicus Curie)
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Dinesh Kumar Mishra
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Rama Shankar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri S.P. Pandey,
learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
Learned counsel for the informant is not present.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 165 of 2018, under Section 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Khora, District Ghaziabad, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

Sukhbir vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66142187/
1 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
The name of the applicant has come up later on in the statement of the arrested co-accused person, which is not admissible in the Indian Evidence Act.
It is stated that as far as co-accused persons are concerned, the matter is of civil nature andthe applicant has nothing to do in the said case.
The applicant was granted interim protection vide order dated 17.2.2020 by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court.
It is stated that final report (charge sheet) has been submitted qua the applicant also, without application of mind.
The applicant has not misused the said opportunity granted.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

5. In support of his submission, learned counsel has placed reliance upon the judgement of the Apex Court in Aman Preet Singh vs. C.B.I. through Director AIR 2021 SC 4154, wherein the Court has clearly held that if a person, who is an accused in a non-bailable/cognizable offence, was not taken into custody during the period of investigation, in such a case, it is appropriate that he may be released on bail as the circumstances of his having not been arrested during investigation or not being produced in custody is itself sufficient to entitle him to be released on bail.

entities.text: Aman Preet Singh vs. C.B.I. through Director AIR 2021 SC 4154
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgement of the Apex Court.
8. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Justice Krishan Pahal) Order Date :- 16.1.2024 Shalini  Sukhbir vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66142187/
